catalogue.final:
Catalogue complete. A second full run of both scripts wrote nothing: the last transaction ID is unchanged and the entity counts held.

## Sources indexed
| Source | Records indexed |
|---|---|
| Shopify | 21,129 customers, 26,546 orders and 37,773 order lines, plus the 49 variants (as hubs) |
| Amazon | 38,264 orders, 43,513 order lines, 49 FBA inbound shipments, 25 listings |
| 3PL | 49 items, 29 receipts, 146 receipt lines, 37,331 outbound lines |
| QuickBooks | 11 vendors (vendor list only; the ledger was not touched) |
| Supplier invoices | 41 commercial invoices, read only for factory item codes, tariff codes and suppliers |

I did not index the inventory snapshot positions, the WeChat chats, the ops inbox, the proforma invoices, or the QuickBooks transaction list. The chats, inbox and proformas belong to the ingestion skill, and the transaction list is the general ledger.

## Crosswalk (49 SKU hubs)
| System | Hubs carrying its ID | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| Shopify variant | 49 | 43 exact, 6 normalized (0.9) |
| 3PL item code | 49 | all exact on UPC (1.0) |
| Amazon seller SKU, ASIN, FNSKU | 25 | 14 exact, 11 normalized by dropping `-FBA` (0.9) |
| Factory item code, supplier, HS code | 49 | all corroborated by description (0.7) |

- **Amazon:** the other 24 hubs are not listed on Amazon. These 25 are the only Amazon SKUs in the orders.
- **Suppliers:** QuickBooks vendors map to 8 supplier codes by the code in their email address (0.9). The other 3 vendors are the forwarder, the customs broker and the 3PL. They have no supplier code, so they sit in the index under their QuickBooks name only.
- **Outbound lines:** every 3PL outbound line resolves to either a Shopify order or an FBA shipment.

## Attributes registered (16)
- **Shopify IDs:** `shopify/order_id`, `shopify/order_name`, `shopify/customer_id`, `shopify/line_item_id`. Order name is what the 3PL cites.
- **Shopify and 3PL SKU spellings:** `shopify/sku` and `tpl/client_sku`. They record each system's own spelling of "SKU".
- **3PL keys:** `tpl/receipt_no`, `tpl/receipt_line`, `tpl/outbound_key`.
- **Amazon IDs:** `amazon/order_id`, `amazon/order_line`, `amazon/inbound_shipment_id`.
- **QuickBooks:** `quickbooks/vendor_name`.
- **Join keys:** `line/sku`, `order/customer`, `receipt/po`.

Field authority is recorded on each system's identifier attributes.

## Duplicates marked
567 Shopify accounts are marked `core/same_as` the oldest account with the same mailbox. They share a mailbox once plus-aliases, dots and case are normalised, and the same full name (confidence 0.9). That is 565 pairs and one triple. Every pair had matching names but often different postcodes, so those people may be using different addresses.

## Where the sources disagree on "SKU"
- **Shopify:** hand-typed, and 6 variants are off-pattern: `AH-CTB-16-LRG`, `AH-JAR-22-STL`, `AH-TPT-23-CLR`, `AH-TRY-18-NAT`, `AHUTN0017NAT`, `ah-btl-0020-blk`. The hub codes use the standard `AH-FAM-NNNN-COL` spelling.
- **3PL:** the client SKU is hand-keyed. It is blank on 6 items and misspelt on 8 (BKL, WTH, SVL, HFL, BMA and similar), so I matched on UPC instead.
- **Amazon:** a `-FBA` suffix on 11 of the 25 seller SKUs.

## For a human to decide
- **Purchase order stubs:** the receipts name 26 POs, so lookups created 26 PO entities holding only their number. The ingestion skill will fill them in. The alternative is dropping `receipt/po` until POs are ingested.
- **Receipts:** 10 of the 29 have no PO reference.
- **Container numbers:** I left them in the source because shipments don't exist yet. Receipts can be joined to shipments once ingestion creates them.
- **The 3PL's "Available":** it equals on-hand minus allocated and still includes damaged units. I did not index it.
- **No records vanished:** this was the first run, so nothing has disappeared from a source yet.

The scripts are in the scratchpad (`hubs.py`, `bulk.py`, `common.py`). Re-running both is safe.

ingest.final:
I ingested all three folders into the fact store. That is 135 supplier PDFs, 157 chat messages that carried facts and all 163 ops-inbox emails. The write ran as 556 transactions, each citing its document. I checked the counts in the store afterwards.

**Documents read**
- **Supplier PDFs:** 48 proforma invoices, 46 inspection reports and 41 commercial invoice / packing lists.
- **Skipped as already read:** none. The catalogue had cited the 41 commercial invoice / packing lists, but only for item and HS codes. Their shipment facts were missing, so I read them.
- **Chats:** the 8 WeChat chats gave 157 messages with facts. I converted their New York timestamps for the PO placed-on dates and for working out which year a date without one falls in.
- **Emails:** 32 booking confirmations (4 of them roll notices), 31 pre-alerts, 7 ETA updates, 30 arrival notices, 30 customs entry summaries and 29 warehouse receipts.

**In the store now**
- **Purchase orders and lines:** 48 purchase orders with 196 lines. Of these, 37 are received, 4 shipped, 5 in production, 1 ready and 1 confirmed.
- **Shipments:** 32 shipments (31 with a house bill, 1 still only booked) with 166 shipment lines. All 29 receipts are recorded as delivered.
- **QC and customs:** 46 inspections and 30 customs entries.
- **Suppliers:** all 8 supplier records were filled in from the proformas.
- **Merged identifiers:** every pre-alert matched exactly one booking, by vessel and voyage plus a shared PO, so each shipment is a single entity.

**Facts written below confidence 1**
- **0.9 (12 facts):** `po/etd` from messages that name the PO and give a date with no year.
- **0.8 (54 facts):** `po/etd` where the PO is only implied, either through a PI number or because the message follows a PI file in the chat.
- **0.8 (43 facts):** `po/status` in_production, from a supplier acknowledging a deposit.
- **Deposit matching:** the deposit messages don't name a PO, so I matched them by the PI's deposit percentage (30%, 40% or 50%) of its total.
- **0.7:** "大货生产中" (production in progress) was only recorded where a single PO was clearly in play. One message was ambiguous and I didn't record it.

**Choices you may want to check**
- **Email hashes:** I hashed each email from its `From ` line up to the next one, minus the blank separator line. If you hash the separator in, the email document hashes will differ.
- **Chat container messages:** I did not record the "container loaded" messages. None names a PO, and every container number appears at confidence 1 in the commercial invoices or pre-alerts. All of them match a document.
- **PO status "sent":** I never asserted it, because the skill's status table doesn't say when.

**Unresolved**
- No unresolved item codes, no HS code differences from the SKUs, no conflicts between pre-alert and invoice quantities, and no chat ETD that disagreed with its proforma.
- Booking PBLXMN2609032 (PO-2026-0023) has not sailed. It was rolled to ETD 6 Oct 2026.

**Gaps in the vocabulary**
- **Price changes:** the supplier increases and rebates (Mingjia +3%, Qisheng +4%, Lanxin +5%, Hetai −2%) have no attribute.
- **Payments:** the deposit and balance payments have no attribute.
- **Warehouse counts:** 74 received/damaged lines have nowhere to go. Two show a short receipt: AH-BWL-0015-CLY on GSF-RCV-000003 (1,680 expected, 1,656 received) and AH-TMB-0019-BLK on GSF-RCV-000008 (576 expected, 552 received). The rest are damaged units on full counts.
- **Other messages and fields:**
  - holiday closures;
  - sample courier AWBs;
  - the ETD slip reasons;
  - the brokerage fee in customs emails.

The scripts and extracted text are in this session's scratchpad.

rerun.final:
I re-ran the catalogue and wrote nothing, because the store already holds every record in the exports. I compared each source's IDs with the store's and found nothing new and nothing missing.

**Records indexed, source against store**
- **Shopify:** 26,546 orders, 37,773 line items and 21,129 customers. All are in the store.
- **Amazon:** 38,264 orders, 43,513 order lines, 49 FBA inbound shipments and 25 inventory listings. All are in the store.
- **3PL:** 37,331 outbound lines, 29 receipts, 146 receipt lines and 49 item codes. All are in the store.
- **QuickBooks:** 11 vendors, all in the store. I did not index the transaction list, since the general ledger is out of scope.
- **Supplier PDFs, WeChat chats and the ops mbox:** I left these alone. Their records, such as purchase orders, shipments, QC reports and customs entries, belong to the ingestion skill. They are already in the store.

**Crosswalk (49 product hubs, keyed on `sku/code`)**
- **Shopify and 3PL:** all 49 hubs carry a Shopify variant ID and SKU, a 3PL item code, a factory item code, a UPC, an HS code and a supplier.
- **Amazon:** 25 hubs carry an Amazon seller SKU, ASIN and FNSKU. The other 24 are not in the Amazon inventory export, so there is nothing to match.
- **3PL client SKU:** 44 hubs carry one.
  - Five items have a blank client SKU in the 3PL snapshot, so the store has none for them: ACMH-10042, 10133, 10140, 10175 and 10350. They are matched by item code instead.
  - Five more client SKUs differ from our code by a typo, for example `AH-EKT-0004-BKL` against `AH-EKT-0004-BLK`. They sit on the hub as the 3PL's own spelling.

**Other results**
- **Duplicates:** 567 duplicate Shopify customer accounts are already marked with `core/same_as`. I found no new ones.
- **Attributes registered:** none. The store's vocabulary already covers every identifier and join key.
- **Records gone from a source:** none. Store and source counts match.
- **Excised people:** none to report.

**Where the sources disagree on a term:** the 3PL's "Client SKU" is a hand-typed code, and Amazon's seller SKU carries suffixes such as `-FBA`. They are already held as separate attributes (`tpl/client_sku`, `amazon/seller_sku`) rather than forced into `sku/code`.

**For you to decide:** nothing. If the 24 products with no Amazon listing should have one, that needs a fresh Amazon export.
